public_rationale: Under the ordinary behavioral reading, the claim is too absolute. The January SETS study reports successful checking and correction using models’ own feedback, with improvements over sampling-only alternatives. That is evidence against never critically assessing an answer. The finding does not establish consciousness, dependable judgment across domains, or spontaneous detection of the particular April Fool’s joke.
limitations: The decisive study was a preprint authored by researchers affiliated with Google.
The method uses explicit checking prompts and repeated calls.
Results vary by model and task.
The event month identifies the capability documented in January; exact experiment execution dates are not supplied.

our_interpretation: Read critical reflection behaviorally: examining material for errors or inconsistencies and using that assessment to improve an answer. This does not require consciousness.
Ever makes this a claim of absent capability. Reliable examples of successful checking can contradict it without establishing general reliability.
Prompting a model to check its work is permitted, but the checking must not merely repeat an externally supplied correction.
Use January 1 through April 4, 2025: the latest completed quarter plus the April context of the ongoing claim.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled tests across contemporary systems find no effective ability to identify errors or inconsistencies and revise answers using their own assessments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporary model demonstrably checks proposed answers and improves them using its own feedback, without being supplied the correct answer or an external error diagnosis.
